originalTitle: Two Russians handed down jail terms for terrorism and spying in Angola
title: Being Good Visitors: A Story from Angola!
content:
Hello from Your African News Reporter!

Hi everyone! It's your friendly news reporter here, coming to you live from our wonderful continent of Africa! Today, we have an important story from a beautiful country called Angola. Have you ever heard of Angola? It's a special place with lots of sunshine and friendly people, right here in Africa! Did you know? Angola is a big country in southern Africa! It has amazing beaches along the Atlantic Ocean and lots of wild animals like elephants and zebras in its national parks. Imagine seeing all those incredible animals! Our story today is about something that happened when some grown-ups visited Angola. It's about how important it is for everyone, even visitors, to follow the rules of a country.

What Happened in Angola?

Once upon a time, not so long ago, two grown-ups came to visit Angola. They were from a country very, very far away called Russia. One of them was like a person who gives advice about how a country should be run, and the other helped people speak different languages understand each other. But something went wrong. These two visitors were accused of doing things that are not allowed. They were accused of breaking some very important rules in Angola. These rules are called 'laws', and they help keep everyone safe and happy in a country. Did you know? Every country in the whole wide world has its own special rules, or laws! These laws are like the rules we have at home or at school. They help us all live together nicely and fairly.

What Does 'Breaking Rules' Mean Here?

The big words they used for what these visitors were accused of are 'terrorism' and 'spying'. Wow, those sound like big, scary words, don't they? But let's break them down simply, so we can understand. When we talk about 'terrorism' in this story, it means they were accused of trying to cause big trouble. Like trying to make people angry and fight, or get them to protest in a way that causes problems for everyone. It's like trying to start a big, noisy argument when everyone should be playing nicely. And 'spying'? Spying is when someone tries to find out secrets that don't belong to them. Imagine if someone tried to secretly read your diary or peek at your friend's secret club plans without asking! That's not fair, right? In this case, it means trying to get secret information about Angola to share with another country, without permission. Did you know? It's always best to be open and honest! If you have something to say or share, it's good to talk about it with kind words, not by trying to cause trouble or take secrets.

Why Are Rules So Important?

Rules, or laws, are super important because they help everyone stay safe and happy. Imagine if there were no rules at school! Everyone might run around, push, and not share toys. It would be very messy and not fun at all! In a country, laws help make sure people don't hurt each other, or steal, or cause big problems. They help us know what is right and wrong, and how we can all live together peacefully. The two visitors said they didn't do these things. They said they were innocent. But a special person called a judge, who helps decide if rules were broken, looked at all the information carefully. Did you know? Judges are like very wise grown-ups who listen to everyone's side of a story and try to make the fairest decision based on the rules. Their job is to help keep justice in the land!

What Happened Next?

After looking at everything, the judge decided that the rules had been broken. So, these two grown-ups were asked to stay in a special place for a while. This is what we call 'jail terms'. It means they have to spend time in a special building to think about what they did and learn from their mistakes. This shows us that no matter who you are, or where you come from, when you visit a new place, you must always respect their rules and their people. It's like when you go to a friend's house – you follow their house rules, right? Did you know? When you travel to a new country, it's a good idea to learn a few words in their language! Saying 'hello' or 'thank you' in their language can make people very happy!

What Can We Learn From This?

This story reminds us of a few very important things. First, always follow the rules! Rules are there to keep us safe and help us get along. Second, be a kind and respectful visitor wherever you go. Whether it's to another country or just to a friend's house, always treat others and their home with respect. And third, if you have something you want to change or share, it's always better to do it through talking, being kind, and working together, not by causing trouble or trying to be secretive. Angola is a wonderful country, and its people deserve to live in peace and safety, just like everyone else. We all want to live in a world where everyone is happy and follows the rules. Did you know? Africa is a continent with 54 different countries! Each one is special and unique, with its own history, culture, and amazing people. How cool is that?

Always Follow the Rules!

So, remember kids, whether you're at home, at school, or visiting a new place, being kind, respectful, and following the rules makes the world a much better place for everyone! That's all for today from your friendly African news reporter. Keep smiling and keep learning!
summary: Two visitors from Russia were asked to stay in a special place in Angola because a judge decided they broke important rules by trying to cause big trouble and find secrets.
whyMatters: This story matters because it teaches us that everyone, even visitors from other countries, must follow the rules (laws) of a place to keep everyone safe, happy, and peaceful.

originalTitle: Mysterious white foam draws crowds on  Nigerian highway
title: A Big Foamy Mystery on Our Road!
content:
Hello, Super Friends!

Hi everyone! It's your friendly reporter, Kiki, here with some exciting news from our amazing country, Nigeria! We have a super interesting story today that will make you wonder and think. Get ready for an adventure of discovery!

A Big Foamy Surprise!

Imagine you are driving with your family, looking out the window. Suddenly, you see something very, very white and bubbly! It's not snow, because we don't have snow here. It's foam! Lots and lots of white foam appeared on a big road near a town called "Greenville Road" in Nigeria. It looked like someone had put a giant washing machine on the highway! The foam was fluffy and high, like big white clouds hugging the ground. People were so surprised when they saw it. Many cars slowed down to look at this funny sight. People were curious! They stopped their cars and stood at the side of the road, pointing and whispering. It was truly a strange and wonderful thing to see.

What is This White Stuff?

So, what was this mysterious white, bubbly stuff? It was a big question mark for everyone! It looked just like the bubbles you see when you wash your clothes with soap or when you have a fun bubble bath. But how did so much of it get onto a big busy road? No one knew the answer right away. It was a real-life mystery, just like in your favorite storybooks! Everyone wondered if it came from a big soap factory, or maybe a truck that was carrying lots of bubbles. Did you know? Bubbles are made when air gets trapped inside a thin layer of liquid. Think about blowing bubbles with a wand! This foam was like millions of tiny bubbles all stuck together.

Keep a Safe Distance, Please!

Now, even though it looked fun and fluffy, our grown-up helpers had an important message for everyone. These helpers are from our country's special team called the "Environmental Protection Agency." They are like superheroes for nature! Their job is to keep our land, water, and air safe and clean for all of us, and for the animals too. They quickly told everyone, "Please, do not go near the white foam! Do not touch it or play in it!" This was a very important warning. Why? Because sometimes, things that look fun can actually be a bit tricky for our bodies. They said the foam could be a "health risk." This means it might make you feel unwell. It could make your skin itch, or maybe give you a tummy ache if you accidentally touched it and then touched your mouth. So, it's super important to listen to these safety helpers!

Why Do We Need to Be Careful?

It's just like when your parents tell you not to touch a hot stove or a sharp knife. We need to be careful with things we don't know about. This white foam was a puzzle, and until we knew what it was made of, it was best to stay far away. Even though it looked like giant marshmallow clouds, it wasn't for playing. Our helpers want to make sure all the children and grown-ups stay healthy and happy. Being careful is being smart! Did you know? Staying safe means listening to grown-ups who know what's best, especially when something new and unknown appears. It's like having a superpower of good listening!

Our Clever Scientists Are Helping!

But don't worry, our clever scientists are on the case! The Environmental Protection Agency sent their super smart scientists to the Greenville Road. These scientists are like detectives, but for nature and things like foam. They put on special gloves and took little pieces of the white foam. They put these pieces into special bottles. They will take them back to their super science lab to study them very, very carefully. They want to find out exactly what the foam is made of. Are there chemicals in it? Is it just soap? Where did it come from? These are all the questions they are trying to answer. It's like a big science experiment to keep everyone safe! Did you know? Scientists use special tools like microscopes to look at tiny things that our eyes can't see! They are like super zoom cameras for very small particles.

How Does Foam Get on the Road?

This is the big question everyone is asking! Sometimes, foam can come from different places. Maybe a truck carrying special soap for cleaning things had a little spill. Or perhaps water from a factory that cleans things got onto the road and started making bubbles. Sometimes, very rarely, even nature can make foam in rivers or oceans, but that's usually different from what was on the road. The scientists will help us find the real story behind this foamy mystery! It's important for us to learn so that we can make sure it doesn't happen again, or if it does, we know what to do.

Keeping Our Earth Clean and Safe

This whole foamy mystery reminds us how important it is to keep our beautiful Earth clean. When things that don't belong get into our environment, it can cause problems for plants, animals, and us! We can all be helpers too! We can always remember to put our rubbish in the bin, and not litter. This helps keep our roads, parks, and rivers clean and sparkling. Every little bit helps! Did you know? Keeping our environment clean helps animals like birds, monkeys, and fish stay healthy in their homes! When our Earth is clean, everyone is happy!

What Happens Next?

After the scientists find out what the foam is, our helpers will know the best way to clean it up safely. They will make sure all the white bubbles are gone from Greenville Road so that it's safe for cars and people again. We will keep listening for more news from our Environmental Protection Agency superheroes. They are working hard to solve this mystery and keep our communities safe.

Stay Curious and Safe!

So, remember, my super friends: it's great to be curious about new things, but always be safe! Listen to your grown-ups and the helpers who work hard to protect our wonderful world. That's all for today's news from Kiki! See you next time!
summary: A mysterious white foam appeared on a road in Nigeria, making everyone curious, but helpers quickly warned people to stay away because it might be unsafe, and now scientists are working to find out what it is and clean it up.
whyMatters: This matters because it teaches us to be careful around unknown things, listen to safety helpers, and reminds us that keeping our environment clean is important for everyone's health and happiness.

originalTitle: Death toll from blast at Indian hydroelectric project rises to 20 people
title: Sad News from India: A Story About Water, Power, and Brave Helpers
content:
Hello, little adventurers! Your friendly news reporter from Africa is here. Today, we have some news from a country far, far away. It's a big country called India. Something sad happened there, and we want to tell you about it gently. It's a story about a place that makes electricity from water, and some brave people who worked there.

A Very Big Power Station

Imagine a super-duper big machine that helps make lights turn on in your home! This machine uses water to do a very important job. It turns the water's power into electricity. We call these places "hydroelectric projects." "Hydro" means water, and "electric" means, well, electricity! They often have big dams that hold back water, like a giant wall. Then, the water flows through special pipes and spins big wheels called turbines. These spinning wheels make electricity! It's amazing how water can help us get power. This electricity helps us watch TV, charge our phones, and light up our schools at night. It is a very important part of our modern world. Without it, many things would not work. **Did you know?** Water power has been used for hundreds of years! Long, long ago, people used water to spin big wheels that would grind corn into flour. Now, we use it to make electricity for millions of homes and businesses!

What Happened in India?

Sadly, at one of these big water-power places in India, something very loud and scary happened. There was a "blast." Imagine a very, very loud bang, much bigger than a firecracker! This blast happened deep inside a long, dark tunnel. Tunnels are like long, hollow pathways dug under the ground or through mountains. People work inside these tunnels to build and fix the big machines that make power. They are very brave workers, helping to bring light and power to everyone. After the blast, things became very dangerous inside that tunnel. The sound was very big and it shook everything. **Did you know?** Tunnels are built for many reasons! Some tunnels let trains and cars go through mountains. Other tunnels carry water or or electricity pipes. Building them is a very tricky and important job that needs lots of care!

Brave Rescuers to the Rescue!

When something bad happens, special people rush to help. We call them "rescuers." Rescuers are like superheroes! They are very brave and very strong. They put on special gear and go into dangerous places to look for people who need help. In India, many rescuers went to the hydroelectric project right away. They wanted to find the workers who were inside the tunnel when the blast happened. They worked very, very hard, day and night, to try and save everyone. They are truly heroes because they risk their own safety to help others. They are trained for these very difficult situations and try their best even when it's super dangerous. **Did you know?** Many countries around the world have special rescue teams. They train very hard to be ready for emergencies like floods, earthquakes, or accidents. They help people feel safe and find their way out of danger!

Big Trouble Inside the Tunnel

The rescuers faced many problems inside the tunnel. It was not easy to get in or find anyone. First, there was a lot of "flooding." Imagine your bathtub overflowing, but with so much water it filled up the long tunnel! This water made it hard to see and hard to move around. It was very messy and dangerous. Second, there was "toxic gas." This is air that is not good to breathe. It's like a bad smell that can make you very, very sick, or even make you stop breathing. You cannot see toxic gas, but it is there, making the air unsafe for anyone. Rescuers need special masks to breathe in such places. Third, parts of the tunnel had "collapsed." This means parts of the roof and walls had fallen down. Imagine building a sandcastle tunnel, and then parts of it cave in. It blocks the path and traps people inside. All these things together made the tunnel a very, very dangerous place for the workers and for the rescuers. It was a race against time. **Did you know?** Water can be very powerful! A small stream can become a raging river during heavy rains. That's why building with water needs to be done very carefully and safely, so it doesn't cause harm.

Sad News for Families

Because of all this danger – the water, the bad air, and the fallen tunnel parts – it was very difficult for the people trapped inside to stay safe. The brave rescuers tried their very, very best for many days. They never gave up hope. But the news from India is very sad. The rescuers now say it is unlikely that anyone trapped inside survived. This means that some people working there lost their lives. So far, about 20 people have been counted. This is called the "death toll." It means 20 people who were working hard to bring light to homes will not go home to their families. We are very sad for all the workers and their families in India. It is a very sad time for them, and we think of them from far away in Africa. We send them our love and hope they find comfort and strength. **Did you know?** Sometimes, even when things are very sad, it's important to talk about them. Sharing our feelings helps us feel better and shows we care about each other, even across oceans.

Learning from Sad Times

Even when sad things happen, we can learn important lessons. This sad event reminds us how important safety is, especially when building big things like power stations or tunnels. It reminds us to always be careful and to make sure places where people work are very, very safe. We must always try our best to protect people and make sure they can go home safely after their work. And it reminds us of the brave hearts of rescuers who never give up helping others. They are truly heroes who teach us about courage and kindness. **Did you know?** Engineers and safety experts work very hard to design and build things like tunnels and power stations to be as safe as possible. They use clever tools and plans to make sure workers are protected and danger is avoided.

Thinking of Our Friends

So, even though India is very far away, we can still think of our friends there. We can send them our kind thoughts and wish them strength during this difficult time. We remember the brave workers who lost their lives while helping to make electricity for everyone. Their work was important, and we honour their memory. And we remember the brave rescuers who tried their very best. We hope that no more sad things like this happen again. Let's all remember to be kind and helpful to each other, no matter where we live in the world.
summary: In India, a big accident happened at a place that makes electricity from water, and sadly, many brave workers lost their lives in a collapsed tunnel filled with water and bad air, making everyone around the world feel sad for their families.
whyMatters: This story helps us remember that making electricity, which we all use, can sometimes be dangerous work, and we must always work hard to keep people safe. It also shows us that people everywhere are connected and care for each other, even when they live far away.
